extracted.intended_audience: Institutional applicants and recipients of NIH Kirschstein-NRSA institutional research training grants (PD/PIs, authorized organizational representatives, business officials, grant administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and requirements for administration, allowable costs, reporting, and conduct of Kirschstein‑NRSA institutional research training grants (T32 and related mechanisms). Covers stipend/tution rules, allowable/unallowable costs, rebudgeting, reporting forms, leave, publications, IP, and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Award Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: While some pre-award costs are allowable to a training grant, recipients should note that stipends and tuition and fees may not be charged to a grant until a trainee has been officially appointed and the appropriate paperwork submitted to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends and tuition/fees may not be charged as pre-award to an institutional training grant. Rarely, costs associated with training-related expenses and/or trainee travel may be allowable as pre-award costs — consult the NIH awarding IC when considering pre-award costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees generally are supported for 12-month full-time training appointments for which they receive a stipend as a subsistence allowance to help defray living expenses during the research training experience. The stipend is not “salary” and is not provided as a condition of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipends must be paid in accordance with established stipend levels; recipient organizations may not negotiate departures from NIH standard stipends with trainees. NIH stipend amounts may be adjusted only at appointment or reappointment and are prorated for appointments of less than 12 months. Postdoctoral stipend level for year 1 is determined by full years of relevant postdoctoral experience; subsequent years follow the next level and do not change mid‑year. Stipends are updated annually in NIH Guide and on NIH Fiscal Policies page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Tuition and Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition and fees are allowable trainee costs only if such charges are applied consistently to all individuals in a similar training status at the organization, without regard to their source of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predoctoral: NIH provides 60% of actual tuition up to $16,000/year (60% up to $21,000 for dual-degree programs). Postdoctoral: 60% of actual tuition up to $4,500/year (or up to $16,000 if enrolled in formal degree-granting postdoctoral training). Tuition and fees are awarded as a lump sum and can be allocated without prior NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training-Related Expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds are provided to defray costs such as staff salaries, consultant costs, equipment, research supplies, staff travel, trainee health insurance, and other expenses directly related to the training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training-related expenses are requested and awarded as a lump sum based on a predetermined amount per trainee. Many allowable costs may cover global program costs where NRSA covers only some trainees; institutions should allocate appropriate portions and apply core cost principles of allocation and consistent treatment. This budget category is finite — institutions must be mindful in allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainee health insurance (self-only or family as applicable) is an allowable trainee-related expense only if such charges are applied consistently to all individuals in a similar training status at the organization, without regard to their source of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health insurance can include vision/dental if consistent with organizational policy. Health insurance is awarded as part of the Training-Related Expenses category and institutions must maintain consistent treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical Liability and Other Special Insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical liability (malpractice) insurance or other special insurance is an allowable cost to NRSA grants only if the nature of the research training requires such special insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the cost to be charged to the NRSA grant, it must be consistently required for all in a similar training status regardless of source of support. Routine optional employee benefit insurances (disability, life, workers’ comp) are not normally allowable unless the nature of training requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Salaries as Training-Related Expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff salaries may be charged as training-related expenses where applicable cost principles apply and the training program may qualify as a 'major project' allowing administrative salaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should follow applicable cost principles when charging staff salaries to training-related expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaker Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When speakers are part of program required for NRSA-supported trainees, a portion of such a cost could be charged as Training-related expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge speaker fees to training-related expenses when speakers are required elements of the training program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meals
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of meals may be allowable if provided in conjunction with a meeting considered an ancillary activity to the training grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A portion of meal costs could be charged as Training-related expenses; institutions should follow Cost Considerations—The Cost Principles for guidance on consistent treatment and reasonableness and have institutional policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Under exceptional circumstances (which can include accommodating the disabilities of a trainee), it is possible to request organizational costs above the standard level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for additional costs must be explained in detail and justified in the application; consultation with NIH program staff in advance is strongly advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Travel Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH awarding IC may provide grant funds to cover trainee travel, including attendance at scientific meetings, which the organization determines is necessary to the individual’s training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainees must be appointed to the training grant at time of actual travel for travel costs to be allowable. Funds may not cover routine travel between residence and training institution except a one-way allowance in extreme hardship. Support for research training away from the recipient organization may be permitted with justification of opportunities and requires prior approval of the NIH awarding IC; letters requesting such training may be submitted at any time during appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for Training Away From Parent Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Research training experiences away from the parent organization may be permitted when justified by the type of opportunities and relation to the trainee’s career stage and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such experiences require prior approval of the NIH awarding IC and must be justified as offering opportunities different from the parent organization; letters requesting approval can be submitted anytime during appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Training Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient may receive up to one-twelfth of the annual amount designated for training-related expenses each month to offset costs for short-term health-professional research training positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly pro rata distribution may be used to support tuition, fees, travel, supplies, and other short-term training expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee Benefits (Unallowable on NRSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because NRSA awards are not provided as a condition of employment, it is inappropriate and unallowable to charge NRSA institutional training grants for costs normally associated with employee benefits (e.g., FICA, workers compensation, life insurance, union dues, unemployment insurance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a trainee requests the institution deduct such a cost from the stipend (e.g., union dues), the institution may provide the service, but deductions cannot be automatic without trainee approval. Follow separate sections on Employee Benefits in the cost principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients, other than State, local, or Indian tribes, will receive indirect costs at 8 percent of modified total direct costs (exclusive of tuition and fees, childcare costs, consortiums in excess of $25,000, and expenditures for equipment) rather than on the basis of a negotiated rate agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State, local, and Indian tribes are eligible for full indirect cost reimbursement. For this policy, State universities or hospitals are not considered governmental agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Childcare costs are allowable for full-time predoctoral or postdoctoral NRSA trainees appointed to the institutional training award prior to use of the childcare costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will provide childcare costs at time of award (new, renewal, continuation). Childcare cost levels are published periodically. Childcare must be provided by a licensed provider; recipients must maintain supporting documentation (proof of license) and make it available to NIH upon request (not required to submit with each request). Childcare costs are not tied to payback obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting—Trainee-Related Expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebudgeting of funds awarded in a lump sum for trainee-related expenses does not require NIH awarding IC prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainee-related lump-sum funds can be reallocated within that category without prior approval, subject to applicable policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting—Trainee Costs (stipends/tuition)
rubrics_metrics.description: For rebudgeting purposes, trainee costs include funds awarded in the stipends or tuition/fees budget categories. These costs may not be used for other purposes except under unusual circumstances and then only with prior approval of the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise restricted, rebudgeting into or within stipends and tuition/fees is allowable without prior approval of the NIH awarding IC; moving trainee costs out requires prior approval under unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebudgeting—Trainee Travel
rubrics_metrics.description: For rebudgeting purposes, trainee travel is not considered a trainee cost and therefore may be rebudgeted into any other budget category without prior approval of the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainee travel funds can be moved to other budget categories without prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend Supplementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may supplement stipends from non-Federal funds provided the supplementation is without any additional obligation for the trainee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations determine amount of supplementation per their established policies which must be consistently applied to all in similar training status regardless of source. Federal funds may not be used for supplementation unless specifically authorized. Individual may use Federal educational loan funds or VA benefits as permitted by those programs. PHS funds may never be used for supplementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation (paid employment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows and trainees may spend on average an additional 25% of their time (e.g., ~10 hours/week) in part-time research, teaching, or clinical employment, so long as those activities do not interfere with or lengthen their NRSA training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds characterized as compensation may be paid only when there is an employer-employee relationship, payments are for services rendered, and conditions in cost principles are met. Compensation must be in accordance with organizational policies consistently applied and supported by accounting records reflecting the employer-employee relationship. Compensation for services (salary, fringe, tuition remission) paid from research grants is allowable under these conditions but must not be for the same research that is part of the trainee’s approved NRSA training experience. PD/PIs must approve employment on research grants to ensure no detriment to training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Income—Concurrent Benefits Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may not receive support under a Kirschstein-NRSA institutional training grant concurrently with another federally sponsored fellowship or similar award that provides a stipend or otherwise duplicates provisions of the NRSA award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent receipt of duplicative stipend/support is prohibited. Specific program exceptions (e.g., MARC-U*STAR Pell grant acceptance) noted elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Income—Educational Loans or GI Bill
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may accept concurrent educational remuneration from the VA (GI Bill) and Federal educational loan funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such funds are not considered supplementation or compensation. Specific program exceptions (e.g., MARC-U*STAR Pell grant acceptance) apply where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Loan Repayment Program Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral trainees may be eligible to participate in the NIH Loan Repayment Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in Loan Repayment Program is permitted; consult program details for eligibility and interaction with NRSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxability of Stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 117 of the Internal Revenue Code applies to the tax treatment of scholarships and fellowships; degree candidates may exclude amounts used for qualified tuition and related expenses; nondegree candidates must report stipends and course tuition/fees as gross income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH takes no position on individual tax status; trainees should consult IRS/local tax authorities. IRS Revenue Procedures clarified student FICA exception but NIH understands those do not apply to Kirschstein-NRSA programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 1099 Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Although stipends are not considered salaries, the funds are subject to Federal and sometimes State taxes; the recipient organization may report such funds on IRS Form 1099.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient organizations are not required to issue Form 1099 but often do as documentation; trainees are required to report NRSA stipends as income regardless of Form 1099 issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Standard Terms of Award apply to NRSA institutional training grants; however, in most cases recipients must obtain awarding IC prior approval to carry over funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some NIH awarding ICs have waived the prior approval requirement for training grants; the NoA will specify whether prior approval to carry over funds is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Income—Application Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for NIH research grants, including NRSA institutional training grants, are required to include in their grant applications an estimate of the amount and source of program income expected to be generated as a result of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Administrative Requirements—Program Income in IIA for governing policies on disposition and reporting of program income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Appointment (Form PHS 2271) — Submission Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must submit a PHS 2271 to the NIH awarding IC before or at the start of each trainee’s appointment or reappointment; the PHS 2271 cannot be submitted until after the NoA for the respective budget period has been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHS 2271 includes biographical data and stipend level; must be submitted electronically via eRA Commons xTrain. Trainees must sign reappointments and amendments. No stipend or other allowance may be paid until the appointment form has been submitted. Interim revisions (name, address, period, stipend) must be reported by PD/PI on amended PHS 2271 with trainee signature via xTrain. ORCID iDs are required and xTrain will check that an ORCID iD is linked before accepting appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payback Agreement (Form PHS 6031)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Payback Agreement covering the initial 12 months of NRSA postdoctoral support must be signed by each postdoctoral trainee; not required if individual already received 12 months of postdoctoral NRSA support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Payback Agreement is required for predoctoral or prebaccalaureate trainees. See Payback Requirements section for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination Notice (Form PHS 416-7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Termination Notice, along with the PHS 2271, is the basis for validating the total period of NRSA support and establishing payback obligation; PD/PI must submit a Termination Notice for each trainee within 30 days of the end of the total period of support even if trainee not available for signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information typically must be verified by the program director and an institutional business official, but if PD/PI unavailable the institutional business official may verify. Submit PHS 416-7 electronically via xTrain. No Termination Notice required for prebaccalaureate (T34) trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPR) for Training Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPRs must be submitted for non-competing continuation support following RPPR instructions; guidance for training grants in section 7.4 of RPPR Instructions. A Final RPPR is required within 120 days after the end of grant support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDP provision in Non-Competing Continuation Progress Reports applies to all trainees reported on PHS 2271; provide information per RPPR instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Financial Report (FFR)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual FFR is required for all NRSA institutional training grant awards no later than 90 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which the budget period ended; the report documents financial status per official accounting records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trainee stipends and tuition are obligated for the full 12-month appointment from the budget period in which appointment is initiated; portions extending beyond budget period are reported as unliquidated obligations. If the FFR covers the final budget period, it must have no unliquidated obligations, must indicate exact unobligated funds balance, and is due within 120 days of the period of performance end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH Closeout requirements apply to NRSA institutional training grants; in addition, Termination Notices for all trainees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Administrative Requirements—Closeout—Final Reports in IIA and ensure PHS 416-7 Termination Notices are submitted as part of closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in the Project—Prior Approval Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in program objectives as they relate to the area of research training for which the grant was approved require prior approval of the NIH awarding IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PD/PI will be absent more than 3 months, conduct plans must be approved in writing by the awarding IC. Proposed change of PD/PI must be requested by recipient and approved in writing after review of nominee’s qualifications. Transfers of NRSA institutional training grants to another domestic organization are generally not permitted except under unusual circumstances and require awarding IC approval demonstrating no negative impact on active trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave Policies (vacation, sick, parental, terminal, unpaid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave durations apply to full-time trainees; trainees may receive stipends during normal vacations/holidays and up to 15 calendar days sick leave per year; up to 60 calendar days parental leave per year for adoption or birth of each child; terminal leave is not permitted; extended leaves require unpaid leave approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time between semesters is considered active research, not vacation. Sick leave may be extended under exceptional circumstances by NIH awarding IC per written request from AOR. Parental leave requires advanced notification to institution; notification must be consistent with organizational policy. Trainees requiring leave beyond specified amounts (>15 sick or >60 parental days) must seek prior approval from NIH awarding component for unpaid leave with AOR and PD/PI signatures. During leave, appointment suspension documentation must be submitted (amended Statement of Appointment and Termination Notice); reappointment documented upon resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of Award
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may terminate an NRSA institutional training grant before its normal completion date if recipient materially fails to comply with terms or to carry out the purpose of the award; NIH will notify recipient in writing with reasons, effective date, and right to appeal. NIH may also terminate at recipient request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations wishing to terminate early must notify NIH awarding IC immediately; NIH will issue revised NoA to specify changed support period and prorated stipends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and Sharing of Research Results
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs and trainees should make results and accomplishments of their NRSA activities available to the research community and public; no restrictions should be placed on publication of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should assist trainees in development and dissemination activities. Trainees are encouraged to publish in journals of their choice. NIH support must be acknowledged in publications with specified language. Public Access Policy applies to articles authored/co-authored by NRSA trainees arising from NIH support. Trainee publications information is included in annual progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright of Supported Works
rubrics_metrics.description: When a publication or similar copyrightable material is developed from work supported by NIH, the author is free to arrange for copyright without NIH approval (except as provided in NoA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any copyrighted materials are subject to a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable license to the Federal government to reproduce, translate, publish, use and dispose of such materials and to authorize others for Federal government purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventions and Patents—NRSA Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: All NRSA institutional training grants and other funding agreements awarded primarily for educational purposes are not subject to invention reporting requirements and NIH has no rights to inventions under those grants and agreements (per 2 CFR 200.315 and 37 CFR 401.1(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRSA training grants are treated differently from research grants for invention reporting and rights; consult cited regulations for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of Professional Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees resulting from clinical practice, professional consultation, or other comparable activities performed pursuant to the purpose of the award may not be retained by the trainee and must be assigned to the recipient organization for disposition per NIH program income policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'professional fees' excludes honoraria, fees for scholarly writing, occasional outside lectures, or advisory service to non-profit organizations; these may be retained by trainee if permitted by organizational policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Policy Requirements and Objectives Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All Public Policy Requirements, Objectives, and Appropriation Mandates discussed in IIA apply to NRSA Institutional programs when appropriate (civil rights; protection of human subjects; inclusion policies; humane care of animals; human embryonic stem cells; recombinant/synthetic nucleic acid, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with applicable policies and procedures; see IIA for complete list and additional application requirements in SF424 (R&R) Section 8 Supplemental Instructions for NRSA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects—Indefinite Involvement Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant organization has an approved FWA or other applicable assurance on file but plans for involvement of human subjects are indefinite at time of application, the assurance number should be provided in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an award is made, human subjects may not be involved until a certification of IRB approval or designation of exemption has been submitted.
